evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts constructor: `@InjectRepository(CourseEntity) private readonly courseRepository: Repository<CourseEntity>`: the enrolments module takes direct database access to the courses table.

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `const courseRepository = this.courseRepository; ... courseRepository.findOne({ where: { id: courseId } })` and `await courseRepository.save(entity)`: course rows are read and saved without going through the courses module's service.

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `const course = toCourse(entity); course.admit(); entity.enrolled = course.enrolled;`: uses courses.service.ts's row-to-Course mapper but copies the result back to the row by hand, here instead of in the courses module.

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts imports `toCourse` from '../courses/courses.service' and `CourseEntity` from '../persistence/entities/course.entity': part of the job of loading and saving courses is split across the two modules.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Injecting a TypeORM Repository<EnrolmentEntity> is the usual NestJS way for a module to reach its own data. No separate enrolments repository is visible, so that part is fine. The problem is that EnrolmentsService also injects Repository<CourseEntity> and reads and saves course rows itself, without going through the courses module's own service. It borrows the mapper toCourse from courses.service.ts to turn a row into a Course, then writes the result back by hand with `entity.enrolled = course.enrolled` and `courseRepository.save(entity)`. So course data is read and changed in two modules, and the rule for mapping a Course back to its database row now lives here as a hand-written copy. Copying the field into a local variable (`const courseRepository = this.courseRepository`) changes nothing: it is still direct database access. This supports the candidate flag: the service handles enrolment rules, course capacity changes and course saving. One more possible issue cannot be confirmed from the source shown: the `studentEmail.includes('@')` check may repeat a check inside the Enrolment domain class. Confidence is moderate because the rubric is worded in terms of "the module's own" abstractions, and this bypass goes around a neighbouring module's abstraction rather than this one's.
